text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- A French parliamentary group met vice president Nguyen Thi Binh on Wednesday to discuss bilateral ties. The meeting comes ahead of November's Francophonie summit in Hanoi.
-- The Vietnam Rubber Corporation, the country's largest producer, is hoping to expand the current 300,000 hectares of plantation nationwide to one million by 2000.
-- Vietnam will actively work towards integration into the international community, cabinet ministers decided at a recent meeting.
-- The Industry Ministry has petitioned the government to ban the export of crude minerals such as kaolin, sand, granite blocks and ilmenite, in order to preserve Vietnam's reserves.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has asked local authorities to reinforce state management at all levels.
-- Burma's Foreign Minister, Ohn Gyaw, arrived in Hanoi on Wednesday for an official visit at the invitation of Vietnamese Foreign Minister Nguyen Manh Cam.
-- Communist Party Secretary General Do Muoi has called for restrictions on imports of outdated technology.
-- Hanoi city reported 12.3 percent gross domestic product growth in 1996.
-- Vietnam's biggest-ever fraud trial began on Wednesday. Eight people have been brought to court, charged with being involved in fraud and appropriation of socialist and citizen's property.
